about.title: Pittsburg Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: When a doctor's visit or surgery in Pittsburg leaves you worse off than expected, the first question is usually whether anyone did something wrong. In California, that question has a precise answer: malpractice means a provider fell below the accepted standard of care, and that failure caused real harm. A disappointing result, by itself, is not enough. Residents here often get care close to home along Railroad Avenue or travel out on SR-4 to larger facilities elsewhere in Contra Costa County, so records can end up scattered across several offices. Gathering those records, having them reviewed by a qualified medical expert, and sending the required 90-day notice before filing suit all take time. California's MICRA rules also set a filing window of generally one year from discovery of the injury, and no more than three years from when it happened. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Pittsburg residents with an independent attorney who handles medical negligence cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Pittsburg Patients Turn to LawProactive

items.title: MICRA deadlines are short and easy to miss
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from the date you discovered the injury, and never more than three years from the injury itself. Getting a case reviewed early keeps those dates from closing on you.

items.title: Notice and expert review are built into the process
items.desc: State law requires a 90-day notice to the provider before a lawsuit is filed, and nearly every claim needs a qualified medical expert to explain how the standard of care was breached. The attorneys in our network handle both from the start.

items.title: The damages cap changes every year
items.desc: California places a statutory cap on non-economic damages in malpractice cases, and that cap rises annually. An attorney who tracks the current figure can explain what it means for a Pittsburg claim like yours.

items.question: My surgery didn't go the way I hoped. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Medicine involves known risks, and a poor outcome on its own does not prove negligence. A claim depends on showing the provider acted below what a reasonably careful professional would have done in the same situation, and that this caused your injury. A qualified medical expert is almost always needed to make that determination.

items.question: I was treated in Pittsburg but also at a hospital outside the city. Where does that leave my claim?
items.answer: That situation is common here, since many residents see a local provider near Railroad Avenue or Harbor Street and are then referred along SR-4 to a larger facility. Your claim follows the negligent act, not your home address, and it can involve more than one provider. An attorney will request records from each location and sort out who was responsible for what.

items.question: How much does it cost to get a Pittsburg malpractice attorney to look at my case?
items.answer: Nothing up front. LawProactive is a free connection service, and the independent attorneys we work with take medical negligence cases on contingency. That means they are paid only if there is a recovery, and the initial review of your records costs you nothing.
